title: Operational Snapshot — SRE Weekly (Nov 3–9, 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Weekly working notes and handoff for the SRE team covering Nov 3–9, 2026. This is a lightweight operational snapshot for on-call, SLO surface, incidents, and immediate action items. Use this doc during Monday sync and push unresolved items to the follow-up agenda.

Highlights (quick):
- Two customer-facing degradations this week; both mitigated without a full outage.
- P95 latency slipped on TextGen API during two short windows (total ~32m).
- Rolling deploy flake observed in autoscaler logic under bursty traffic — root cause investigation started.
- Completed chaos test for kv-cache eviction; notes below.

Incident summaries (brief):
1) INC-2026-384 — Tokenizer memory leak (affecting gpt-compat models)
   - Timeline: Nov 4 03:18 UTC — Nov 4 04:05 UTC (detection -> mitigation)
   - Symptoms: Elevated host memory on serving nodes, increased OOM kills in model-worker pods, increased tail latency for requests requiring fresh tokenization.
   - Impact: Elevated P95/P99 for ~12% of traffic to hosted-textgen in us-west; a small % of requests retried by client SDK. No data loss.
   - Mitigation: Temporarily disabled tokenization cache sharing in the kernel; rolled back a recent tokenizer change (PR #1287) to a canary subset, scaled up affected pool by +2 nodes for 30m.
   - Next steps: Root cause postmortem assigned (SRE-842). Reproduce locally with the fuzz harness and add unit test for tokenizer caching lifecycle.

2) INC-2026-389 — Autoscaler thrash during spot preemptions
   - Timeline: Nov 7 14:05 UTC — Nov 7 14:40 UTC
   - Symptoms: Rapid scale-in triggered by spot preemptions, followed by aggressive scale-out; scaling cooldowns not respected by combined policy (vertical + horizontal mix).
   - Impact: Short latency spikes (P95 up to 720ms) for embedding routes for ~25 minutes; some rate-limited requests returned 429 while autoscaler converged.
   - Mitigation: Eng infra temporarily pinned dedicated pools to non-spot instances for high-priority customers; tweaked cooldown windows.
   - Next steps: Rework autoscaler policy: SRE + infra to propose a single-source-of-truth scaling controller (OPS-1294).

SLO status (week snapshot):
- TextGen API latency (P95 target 250ms): 98.7% (target 99.5%) — regression driven by INC-2026-384 windows and autoscaler thrash.
- Embeddings request success rate (99.9% target): 99.93% — within target overall but with transient 429 clusters during autoscaler convergence.
- System availability (global): 99.992% for the week.

Action items and owners (short):
- Aanya: Draft RCA for INC-2026-384 and link fuzz harness results into SRE-842 (due Nov 12).
- Miguel: Propose autoscaler consolidation plan and timeline; coordinate with infra and product for restricted rollout (due Nov 17).
- Priya: Update runbooks for tokenizer cache failures — add clear detection playbook and temp mitigations (due Nov 15).
- Liam: Add an alert for sustained P95 > 300ms across textgen tier for 10m with paging escalation to on-call (done: alert created, waiting review).
- On-call rotation: ensure next handoff includes notes on which pools were pinned to non-spot (see rotation notes).

On-call and handoff notes (this week's rotation):
- Week on-call: Nov 3–9: Primary on-call: Miguel (primary), Backup: Priya.
- Handoff doc link: slack://thread/GC12345/handoff-nov-3-miguel (referenced in linked_artifacts).
- Handoff highlights to pass forward:
  - Keep an eye on tokenizer-related memory trends; alert threshold lowered to 70% host mem for model-worker nodes.
  - If autoscaler thrash returns, pin high-priority pools to non-spot and open an incident bridge.

Recent changes / Deploys this week (affecting SRE):
- Nov 3: Deploy of tokenization refactor (PR #1287) — rolled to canary then rolled back after INC-2026-384.
- Nov 5: Bumped autoscaler cooldown defaults in staging (PR #1299) — testing in canary.
- Nov 6: Eviction tests for kv-cache (chaos) completed; minor race condition observed when eviction and concurrent compact occur.

Notes from chaos run (kv-cache eviction):
- Test: simulated cache pressure across 1200 parallel requests for 15m with random eviction jitter.
- Observation: under simultaneous compaction+eviction, a small % of requests hit stale cache pointers leading to transient 503s for <1m windows.
- Action: add mutex around compaction path; follow-up PR planned (infra#1315).

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Increased use of larger context windows may exacerbate memory pressure on tokenizer and kv-cache -> mitigation: capacity planning meeting scheduled (Nov 11).
- Risk: Multiple concurrent scaling policies (spot + dedicated + burst) cause instability -> mitigation: emergency policy freeze until consolidation design reviewed.

Meeting notes (SRE weekly sync — Nov 9):
- Attendees: Aanya, Miguel, Priya, Liam, Sarah (infra), Jae (serving runtime)
- Key points:
  - Prioritize tokenizer RCA and run the fuzz harness against the last three tokenizer patches.
  - Autoscaler consolidation is high priority for Q4; surface cost/latency tradeoffs to product.
  - Agreement to add a short-lived feature flag mechanism for tokenization changes so rollbacks are faster.
- Parking lot / follow-ups:
  - Need clearer telemetry for per-model memory use. Sarah to propose telemetry fields by Nov 13.

Quick checklist for next on-call handoff:
- [ ] Ensure pinned pools list is documented and accessible (Miguel)
- [ ] Verify alert thresholds for tokenizer memory and P95 (Liam)
- [ ] Attach fuzz harness logs to SRE-842 (Aanya)
- [ ] Confirm canary config for autoscaler changes (Priya and Sarah)

Questions for leadership / decisions needed:
- Approve temporary budget for a small pool of non-spot reserved capacity for critical customer SLAs (~3 nodes for 3 months) to reduce risk during autoscaler rewrite. (Requested by SRE on Nov 9).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc light; move formal RCA to Confluence and link from here once ready.
- If you are reading during handoff: ping me on slack @aanya with the word "tokenizer" to surface the tracker quickly.

End of snapshot.
